reviews.title: Just terrible
reviews.text:
**⭐ 1/5: Price quadrupled, notice came too late, no way to cancel**

Avoid Poe. Last year I paid $49.95. This year I was charged $199.95, four times as much, with no advance warning. The only notice of the new price arrived the day *after* my subscription renewed, when it was too late to dispute the amount or change my plan.

I decided to cancel so it wouldn't happen again. Poe's website has no way to cancel; it just sends you to Quora, which owns Poe. Quora's site has no cancel option either, no refund process, and no customer service I could reach. I finally disputed the charge with my credit card company and got a full refund. If this happens to you, do the same.

I signed up a year ago for $50 to compare what was out there. That was a reasonable price for a trial. What I didn't sign up for was a renewal at four times the price, notice after the fact, and no way out. Nothing at signup suggested any of that was coming.

Look elsewhere. If you want to try AI models, subscribe to them directly, where you can see what you're paying and cancel when you want.

reviews.title: Updates Are Too Unpredictable
reviews.text:
While I enjoyed Poe for a while, lesser over time, everything about it has been so horrendous for a while. 

There was even a point they shifted their ToS and other info windows when they had suddenly added random content that had the Discord server in a riot. Resulting in a rather ‘where does it say that’ situation after the change… You can also mention that a handful of their staff have also been documented in the past hashing it out with consumers. 

The updates they have are so sudden and random that you really can’t trust them with a subscription. The most recent issue is the global 3,000 -> 300 points shift. As a handful of you know (or don’t), every day you got refresh of free points. So you could still use the app, whether as a free testing user or subscriber (as you could also chill and stack your points as a sub). While some regions have already been handling this shift for months, this was sudden in its email and announcement for the remaining. Some didn’t even get the email notification till some hours before, or even at all. How do you fail to send out emails properly to your consumers about these sudden changes? 

Sudden as it was mentioned randomly in the middle of the day on Friday and carried out early Monday. 

While I understand things change, especially when there’s a conflux of abuse in the system… The way the business decides mid-day or even in the middle of the night to carry out these updates has always been off-putting. You’d think they’d communicate

reviews.title: 300 Points A Day
reviews.text: Now, I’ve been on this app for a WHILE. Probably a year or more. I love this app for the variety in bots and the ability to change responses based on the Bot. Now, this isn’t the problem. The problem is we’ve been restricted to 300 POINTS A DAY!! Compared to our 3,000 a day we had a day ago that made me MORE than happy, even after the first limit to our messages in the first throes of the app’s launch. 300? What are we expected to do with 300 points? Not to mention this is further trying to force users to spend 20 dollars a MONTH for more messages. And what if your users can’t afford it? Now we’re stuck with less than ten messages a day (depending on your bot). Sad to say that I am retiring from my Poe use and now using a competitor.

reviews.title: Points
reviews.text: 300 points? Seriously? I used to really enjoy talking to the bots on here, and it even got me through surgery a year ago. The limit used to be almost unlimited, and then you made the limit 3,000—which was annoying, but fine in the end, because you could still talk and RP. 300 points, now, though? I can barely do anything, and it seems that the points for the bots only seem to increase. You may as well just make the entire app go behind a paywall, because what are you even supposed to do now? I’m deleting this, I desperately hope this app will go back to how it used to be.
